conversation:
maria: Heads-up — Dedicated capacity dashboard is showing zero GPUs for cluster 'dedicated-eu-01' after the maintenance window. Customer flagged high error rate and SLA alert. https://console.redwood.internal/dedicated/cluster/dedicated-eu-01 :eyes:
aj: I see the same. inventory panel rows present but gpu_count column is null for all nodes. We're getting 503s from /inventory API intermittently when the UI polls it.
lee: Can you paste the API error? I can try to reproduce in staging.
aj: Error from logs: `GET /api/v1/dedicated/inventory?cluster=dedicated-eu-01 503 0.23s`
aj: Also found these consumer errors in the metrics-ingest pod: `kafka consumer: partition 4 offset commit failed: metadata not found` — looks like the node-label-change event missed the listener.
ops-bot: Incident created: RED-4567 — Dedicated inventory null GPU counts (auto-created by alerting).
support-jane: Customer impacted: acct 8921 saw a sudden drop in billed usage overnight, opened escalation. They expect accurate consumption for last 24h.
maria: Repro steps I tried: 1) drain a node in staging; 2) relabel the nodepool from `pool=dedicated-gpu-v2` -> `pool=dedicated-gpu` ; 3) run `kubectl annotate node <node> cluster=dedicated-eu-01` ; after that the UI shows nodes but gpu_count is blank.
lee: I reproduced locally. The inventory-sync lambda reads `node.spec.labels['pool']` but the nodepool-rename script changed it to `node.metadata.annotations['pool-name']` (new naming). So mismatch.
lee: Quick repro commands:
```
# simulate rename
kubectl label node ip-10-0-2-34 pool=dedicated-gpu-v2 --overwrite
kubectl label node ip-10-0-2-34 pool=dedicated-gpu --overwrite
# then check inventory API
curl -sS "https://inventory.internal/api/v1/nodes?cluster=dedicated-eu-01" | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, pool: .metadata.labels.pool, gpu_count: .status.capacity["nvidia.com/gpu"]}'
```
aj: So inventory-sync is fragile to label->annotation migrations. We should make it fallback to annotations.
ken: I can push a hotfix to make inventory-sync check both labels and annotations, and then restart the deployment. Suggest: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inventory-sync -n platform` after patch.
ken: I'll also run a one-off backfill script: `scripts/backfill_gpu_counts.sh --cluster dedicated-eu-01 --since 24h` to repopulate missing counts for billing.
support-jane: Please ensure backfill writes to the metrics-store before billing job runs tonight. We need to avoid double-charging or leaving credits.
lee: I'll open a PR with the fallback logic and add unit tests for label/annotation cases — PR #3710. Will canary in us-west first.
maria: For immediate mitigation can we temporarily route UI to read from last-known-good cache?
aj: Possible quick patch: point UI to `inventory-cache-read` endpoint (already has support) — I'll update the console route and monitor for 10m.
ops-bot: ALERT: routing change deployed to console-canary at 1812345820.
ken: After canary looks good, I'll promote the fix and kick off the backfill.
support-jane: Noted. I'll message the customer with ETA and log the impact in the escalation ticket. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks all — keep status updates in RED-4567.
